name: Phase-Field Crystal
desc: A Swift-Hohenberg phase-field crystal resolved to the atomic column: a hexagonal lattice nucleates out of the melt into misoriented grains stitched together by dislocation arrays, while wandering molten pools eat the crystal and it refreezes behind them and the lattice constant breathes so dislocations must climb forever; rendered as a dark-field HRTEM plate, warm bright-field with Fresnel-rimmed atom cores, an ironbow thermal map, or a blueprint of the bare defect network.

energy.doc: contrast and glow of the atom columns and the defect network (higher = hotter, harder)

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the specimen - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: integration steps/frame + how fast the melt pools wander (0.2 still evolves)

density.doc: quench depth = how much of the field holds a crystal (0 = mostly molten, 1 = fully solid, dense with atoms)

melt.doc: amplitude of the wandering quench field - how aggressively molten pools carve through the lattice

grain.doc: film tooth / detector noise over the plate

hue.doc: accent hue of the defect network; atom columns take its complement

x.doc: pan across the specimen when magnified

y.doc: pan down the specimen when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: dark-field electron micrograph / warm transmitted bright-field / ironbow false-colour / blueprint of the defect network alone

seed.doc: deterministic quench - re-nucleates the whole specimen
